cases.state: seeded fixture; the agent is told the first attempt may already have landed
setup: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM RETRY") | .aff_campaign_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 campaign delete {} --force
cases.ask: create a campaign named EVAL IDEM RETRY with payout 3.50 and url https://example.com/idem-retry. My connection dropped on an earlier attempt so this may be a retry — make sure it cannot end up created twice.

checks.run: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM RETRY")] | length'

expected.rubric: PASS if the agent passed --idempotency-key on the create and exactly one campaign exists. FAIL if it created the campaign without a key, or if two rows exist.

cleanup: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM RETRY") | .aff_campaign_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 campaign delete {} --force
cases.notes: The retry-safe path is opt-in: without --idempotency-key a repeated create silently duplicates. An agent that is told a request may be a retry has to reach for the key.

cases.state: seeded fixture; the agent creates two different campaigns in one turn
setup: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM ALPHA" or .aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM BETA") | .aff_campaign_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 campaign delete {} --force
cases.ask: create two campaigns for me, both retry-safe: EVAL IDEM ALPHA with payout 1.25 at https://example.com/idem-alpha, and EVAL IDEM BETA with payout 2.75 at https://example.com/idem-beta

checks.run: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM ALPHA" or .aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM BETA") | "\(.aff_campaign_name)|\(.aff_campaign_payout)"'
p202 campaign list --all --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM ALPHA" or .aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM BETA")] | length'

expected.rubric: PASS if both campaigns exist with their own values. FAIL if the agent sent one idempotency key for both creates and stopped at the 422, leaving BETA uncreated, or if it dropped the key entirely after the refusal instead of minting a second one.

cleanup: p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM ALPHA" or .aff_campaign_name=="EVAL IDEM BETA") | .aff_campaign_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 campaign delete {} --force
cases.notes: A key identifies one operation. Reusing it for a different body is a 422, so an agent that mints one key per turn rather than one per create gets stuck on the second one — the error names the remedy (send a new key), and the agent has to follow it.

cases.state: a fresh click on EVAL Campaign B carrying sale EVAL-IMP-A ($7.25) and its reversal, both recorded by an earlier `p202 conversion import`; /tmp/p202-eval-import.csv holds those two rows plus a new sale EVAL-IMP-B ($3.10) on the same click
setup:
c=$(p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL Campaign B") | .aff_campaign_id' | head -1) && pub=$(p202 tracker list --all --json | jq -r --arg c "$c" '[.data[] | select((.aff_campaign_id|tostring)==$c)][0].tracker_id_public') && url=$(p202 config show --json | jq -r '.url') && before=$(p202 click list --aff_campaign_id "$c" --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.data[0].click_id') && curl -fsS -o /dev/null -A 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0 Safari/537.36' "$url/tracking202/redirect/dl.php?t202id=$pub" && after=$(p202 click list --aff_campaign_id "$c" --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.data[0].click_id') && test "$after" != "$before" && printf 'subid,payout,transaction_id
%s,7.25,EVAL-IMP-A
%s,-7.25,EVAL-IMP-A
' "$after" "$after" > /tmp/p202-eval-import-earlier.csv && p202 conversion import /tmp/p202-eval-import-earlier.csv --force --json >/dev/null && printf 'subid,payout,transaction_id
%s,7.25,EVAL-IMP-A
%s,-7.25,EVAL-IMP-A
%s,3.10,EVAL-IMP-B
' "$after" "$after" "$after" > /tmp/p202-eval-import.csv
cases.ask: Our network sent its conversions export again as /tmp/p202-eval-import.csv (subid, payout, transaction id). Part of it was imported last week. Import it so every sale and reversal is recorded exactly once, and tell me what was new.

checks.run: id=$(sed -n 2p /tmp/p202-eval-import.csv | cut -d, -f1); p202 click conversions "$id" --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.deleted | not) | [.transaction_id, (.amount | tonumber)]] | sort == [["EVAL-IMP-A", -7.25], ["EVAL-IMP-A", 7.25], ["EVAL-IMP-B", 3.1]]'

expected.rubric: PASS if the agent imported the file with `p202 conversion import`, the click ends with sale EVAL-IMP-A, its reversal and sale EVAL-IMP-B once each, and the reply says the two earlier rows were already recorded and one sale was added, from the command's own answer. FAIL if any row was recorded twice, if the agent recorded the rows one at a time some other way without checking the click's conversions, or if it reports counts it did not read.

cleanup: id=$(sed -n 2p /tmp/p202-eval-import.csv | cut -d, -f1); [ -n "$id" ] && printf '%s\n' "$id" | p202 conversion delete-subids - --force --json >/dev/null; rm -f /tmp/p202-eval-import.csv /tmp/p202-eval-import-earlier.csv
cases.notes: `p202 conversion import` (no page; POST /conversions per row, after reading each click's GET /clicks/{id}/conversions). A write run always reads the click's conversions first, and that read is what recognises the sale and the reversal already on file, so this case fails when the CLI cannot read the ledger: the importer once decoded `amount` as a string, and when the API began answering it as a number every row on a converted click failed, which only a run against a real server could show. The check compares amounts with tonumber, so it holds for a server that sends them either way.
